issues.description: The solution defines the pixel-setting routine with the label '.set_pixel' but the template and main code call 'set_pixel' (without a leading dot). This symbol-name mismatch will cause linkage/undefined-symbol errors and prevents the program from assembling/linking as intended, blocking students from running or testing the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the routine name consistent between template/main and the solution. Rename the label in the solution from '.set_pixel' to 'set_pixel' (remove the leading dot), or change the call sites to 'call .set_pixel'. Ensure the exported symbol name matches the call so the assembler/linker can resolve it.

issues.description: The subroutine intended to implement the same concept is named differently: the problem statement and the template declare/call set_pixel, but the solution defines the routine as .set_pixel (leading dot). This creates a mapping confusion for students trying to match the required subroutine name to the provided correct implementation and may obscure how the call in main relates to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution routine from .set_pixel to set_pixel (remove the leading dot) so the implementation identifier matches the name used in the problem statement and the template. Alternatively, make the template and problem refer to the same dotted name, but keeping set_pixel (no dot) is clearer and consistent.
